chunks: Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim b. Hashim, from Muhammad b. Abi Umayr. He said: One who heard Aba Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrated to me that he said:

One who disobeys Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, does not truly love Him. Then he recited: You disobey God yet you manifest your love for Him -- this is impossible, a strange thing in conduct. Had your love been sincere, you would have obeyed Him, for surely the lover is obedient to the one he loves.

key_terms.المحب: Al-Muhibb -- the lover; one who truly loves
key_terms.مطيع: Muti' -- obedient; one who complies out of love

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the relationship between loving God and obeying Him?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) teaches that true love for God is demonstrated through obedience, not mere verbal claims. He then recites famous Arabic poetry that exposes the contradiction of disobeying God while claiming to love Him. The original audience understood this as a direct rebuke of those who professed love for God and the Ahlulbayt while failing to follow divine commands. The verse cited is attributed to the poet Rabi'a al-Adawiyya or other early ascetics, and became a cornerstone of Islamic ethical literature.
word_analysis: may Allah have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (rh) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim b. Hashim from Muhammad b. Abi `Umayr. He said: One who heard Aba `Abdillah al-Sadiq (as) heard him saying:

One who disobeys Allah does not love him. Then, he recited: You disobey God yet you manifest your love for Him. This is impossible. Had you loved Him, you would have obeyed Him. Surely, the lover obeys the one he loves.
